xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3744: Conversation view shows 'How can I help you' empty-state instead of a loading skeleton while the transcript loads

plan.title: Conversation view shows 'How can I help you' empty-state instead of a loading skeleton while the transcript loads
plan.author: agent:k3[1m]

narratives.Problem: On the WebSocket stream path, before the first transcript payload arrives the messages query cache is empty: isLoading is false (the fetch query is disabled), isDiscovering is false, and hasTimelineActivity is false, so isFirstMessage (ConversationPanel.tsx:1308) evaluates true and the panel renders the 'How can I help you?' greeting — an assertion that the conversation is empty — while the truth is 'transcript not delivered yet'. Under server load (PAN-3743) that window stretches to many seconds of wrong information.
narratives.Proposal: Surface a receivedFirstPayload boolean from useConversationMessagesStream (hook-local useState flipped in the WS subscription callback, reset on conversation.name change — never a query-cache sentinel), thread it into ConversationView as a prop, derive awaitingFirstPayload = streamMessagesEnabled && !receivedFirstPayload && messages.length === 0, exclude that state from isFirstMessage / messagesFetchFailed / isOrphaned, and render a message-shaped skeleton (shared by the fetch and stream loading paths) until the first payload arrives.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No changes to the transcript RPC server, the WS protocol, or PAN-3743 queueing work (the load itself is out of scope; this issue only fixes what renders during the wait).
- No change to useSubagentTranscript or the subagent transcript panel.
- No redesign of the greeting, orphaned, spawn-failed, or fetch-failed states beyond gating them on awaitingFirstPayload.
- No skeleton for non-stream (fetch-path) conversations beyond reusing the same skeleton component for the existing isLoading branch — no new fetch-path behavior.

autoDecisions.summary: Change the hook's return shape from boolean to { enabled, receivedFirstPayload } and update both consumers (ConversationPanel.tsx:188, SimpleActivityFeed.tsx:49) in the same commit.
autoDecisions.rationale: A second parallel hook would re-subscribe or duplicate state; a shape change is the smallest honest contract and typecheck pins both call sites. SimpleActivityFeed ignores the new flag.

autoDecisions.summary: receivedFirstPayload is hook-local useState reset on conversation.name change, not a query-cache sentinel.
autoDecisions.rationale: Cache entries survive conversation switches, so a cache sentinel would reintroduce the stale-greeting flash the issue's FR-3 forbids.

autoDecisions.summary: The gating item renders the existing conversationConnecting block for the awaiting state; the skeleton visual lands as a follow-up item replacing it for both loading paths.
autoDecisions.rationale: Keeps the gating item independently mergeable and reviewable; the skeleton item is then a pure visual swap.

autoDecisions.summary: Stream-path tests mock ../../lib/wsTransport (fake getTransport().subscribe capturing the event listener) with agent- prefixed conversation names instead of mocking the stream hook.
autoDecisions.rationale: The hook's own gating (agent- name, stream-capable harness, sessionAlive) is part of the behavior under test; mocking wsTransport exercises the real hook end to end. Existing fixtures use 'test-conv' so they stay on the fetch path untouched.

items.title: Extend useConversationMessagesStream to expose receivedFirstPayload

verify_commands: cd src/dashboard/frontend && bun run vitest run --configLoader runner src/components/chat/__tests__/useConversationMessagesStream.test.ts
expected_outputs: useConversationMessagesStream.test.ts passes including the new receivedFirstPayload cases

narrative.Action: In src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/chat/useConversationMessagesStream.ts, change useConversationMessagesStream to return { enabled, receivedFirstPayload } instead of boolean. Add const [receivedFirstPayload, setReceivedFirstPayload] = useState(false); inside the subscription event callback (currently lines 165–168, the queryClient.setQueryData block) call setReceivedFirstPayload(true); reset it to false when conversation.name changes — the subscription useEffect (lines 157–174) already keys on conversation.name, so reset inside that effect before subscribing. Do NOT derive this from the query cache (a cache sentinel survives conversation switches and would reintroduce the stale-greeting flash, FR-3). Update both consumers in the same commit: ConversationPanel.tsx:188 becomes `const { enabled: streamMessagesEnabled, receivedFirstPayload } = useConversationMessagesStream(conversation);` and SimpleActivityFeed.tsx:49 becomes `const { enabled: streamEnabled } = useConversationMessagesStream(conversation);` (SimpleActivityFeed ignores the new flag). Extend src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/chat/__tests__/useConversationMessagesStream.test.ts with hook-level cases: no event → false; one event → true; conversation-name change → false again. The tests need a vi.mock of ../../lib/wsTransport whose fake getTransport().subscribe captures the event listener so the test can invoke it on demand (see PRD decision D5).

narrative.Action: In src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/chat/ConversationPanel.tsx, thread the new flag into ConversationView: add receivedFirstPayload={receivedFirstPayload} beside streamMessagesEnabled at line 1036, and add receivedFirstPayload?: boolean to ConversationViewProps (declared around line 1162; the ConversationView signature is at line 1175). In the state derivation block (lines 1290–1317), add `const awaitingFirstPayload = streamMessagesEnabled && !receivedFirstPayload && messages.length === 0;` directly above isDiscovering (line 1290). Then add `!awaitingFirstPayload` to all three derivations that treat 'no data yet' as settled: isFirstMessage (line 1308), messagesFetchFailed (lines 1314–1316), and isOrphaned (line 1317). In the render branches, extend the loading branch at line 1345 to `isLoading || isDiscovering || awaitingFirstPayload` so the awaiting state renders the existing conversationConnecting block ('Loading…' / 'Discovering conversation…' — a stream-awaiting conversation may render either label; the skeleton item replaces this visual next). The greeting branch at line 1430 must be unreachable while awaitingFirstPayload is true. Do not touch isSpawning, isSpawnFailed, isForking, or the data?.error branch.

verify_commands: cd src/dashboard/frontend && bun run vitest run --configLoader runner src/components/chat/__tests__/ConversationPanel.test.tsx
expected_outputs: ConversationPanel.test.tsx passes with the three new stream-path cases and all pre-existing tests unmodified

narrative.Action: In src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/chat/__tests__/ConversationPanel.test.tsx, add a stream-path suite. The file currently never mocks the stream hook and its mockConversation is named 'test-conv' (line 83), which keeps shouldStreamConversationMessages false — leave those fixtures alone. For the new suite: (1) vi.mock ../../lib/wsTransport with a fake getTransport() whose subscribe captures the event listener into a test-accessible variable and returns an unsubscribe no-op; (2) build a mock conversation with an agent- prefixed name (e.g. 'agent-test-stream'), sessionAlive: true, endedAt: null, and a stream-capable harness so shouldStreamConversationMessages returns true (check getHarnessBehavior for the harness the fixture needs — mirror whatever makes the pure-function tests in useConversationMessagesStream.test.ts pass). Cover three cases: (a) no event delivered → the skeleton/loading block renders and 'How can I help you?' never appears; (b) invoke the captured listener with one event producing an empty transcript ({ messages: [], workLog: [] }) → the greeting renders; (c) FR-3 reset: render conversation A with no event, rerender with a different agent- name, assert the loading block renders again and the greeting never flashes during the switch. Run only this file with the frontend vitest runner; the whole suite must pass with no pre-existing test modified.

Document the conversation panel's loading and empty states

narrative.Action: Two documentation touches, no behavior change. (1) docs/ISSUE-VIEW.md: in the conversation-view section, add a short paragraph enumerating the panel's loading/empty states and what each asserts — awaiting-first-payload skeleton (transcript not yet delivered; says nothing about emptiness), greeting 'How can I help you?' (first payload received, genuinely empty live conversation), 'Starting…' (spawn window), orphaned / no saved history (ended session, data loaded, no activity), fetch-failed with Retry (request failed; history may be intact). (2) ConversationPanel.tsx: update the state-derivation comment block around lines 1290–1317 so the incident comments (PAN-3544 at 1291–1297, spawn-window at 1299–1305) are joined by a PAN-3744 comment stating that the pre-first-payload window is a loading state, not an empty state, and that receivedFirstPayload is hook-local because the query cache survives conversation switches.
